correctness.rationale: The inspected C census enumerates all 3125^2=9,765,625 ordered transition pairs, performs exact BFS in the 32-subset power automaton, records the first reachable subset omitting each state, and tests singleton reachability for synchronization. Its deterministic output gives 8,063,385 synchronizing pairs and histogram ending in exactly 960 threshold-eight pairs. Canonicalization enumerates all 5! state permutations and optional letter swap. The Python verifier recompiles/reruns the census, checks byte-for-byte output, verifies the four representatives, their exact avoidance vectors, four disjoint 240-element symmetry orbits, and A_5 membership. An independent replay of the four representatives/orbits reproduced the avoidance vectors and orbit sizes. The finite claim is exhaustive, not extrapolated.

value.rationale: This is the complete extremal classification at the first published exceptional five-state threshold, not merely a verification of A_5. The exact multiplicity and three additional symmetry classes are natural finite extremal data for the avoiding-threshold problem and provide reusable test cases for general conjectures.
residual_risks: An older unpublished experimental data set could contain the same four-class census without being indexed.

final_claim: Among all ordered labeled binary complete deterministic automata on five states, the largest 1-avoiding threshold among synchronizing automata is 8; exactly 960 pairs attain it and they form exactly four classes under simultaneous state relabeling and letter interchange, with the published A_5 in the third class.
scientific_limitations: An older unpublished experimental data set could contain the same four-class census without being indexed.
The theorem is only for binary automata on exactly five states and gives no new all-n upper bound.
